chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halby, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who catches the funeral procession while he is not in a state of ablution. If he goes to perform ablution, the prayer upon it will be missed. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should perform tayammum and pray.'

key_terms.الْجِنَازَةُ: Funeral procession or the funeral prayer itself

ai.seo_question: What should one do if they miss the start of the funeral prayer due to lack of ablution?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes tayammum as a valid substitute for wudu in this specific context, prioritizing the communal obligation of joining the funeral prayer over the preferred state of purity. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding ritual purity when time is critical, ensuring the deceased is not left without the prayers of the living. It underscores the principle that the necessity of participating in the congregational act outweighs the minor defect of using dust instead of water.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked about the man who attends the funeral and he is upon (a state) other than ablution. So if he were to go and perform ablution, the Salaat upon it would be missed. Heasws said: ‘He should perform Tayammum and he should pray Salaat’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about a man who attends Salah (prayer) for a deceased without Wudu’ and if he goes for Wudu’ he misses Salah (prayer). He (the Imam) said, ‘He can take Tayammum, then perform Salah (prayer).”’
